title: How Europe deter Russia attacks | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Liana Fix argues Russia's hybrid attacks across Europe (drones, airspace breaches, sabotage, assassination plots) are escalating while U.S. commitment wavers, and that Europe must shift from fragmented national responses to a coordinated asymmetric campaign. She proposes four levers: enabling Ukraine's deep strikes into Russia, seizing shadow-fleet tankers, using frozen Russian assets, and expanded NATO exercises and signaling, plus new EU counter-hybrid mechanisms.

insights.claim: Europe has treated Russian attacks as separate country-by-country incidents handled by national law enforcement, and should instead pivot to a coordinated Europe-wide campaign that builds asymmetric leverage rather than responding in kind.

insights.so_what: A coordinated EU response implies new pressure tools targeting Russian economic vulnerabilities.

insights.claim: The most important lever is Ukraine: Europe should boost support and enable Ukraine to expand its deep-strike campaign into Russia, explicitly linking this to Russia's escalation toward Europe, with U.S. intelligence cooperation.
insights.speaker: Liana Fix
insights.so_what: Expanded Ukrainian deep strikes into Russia raise risk to Russian energy infrastructure and output.
insights.quote: European governments should boost support for Ukraine generally and also enable it to expand its deep-strike campaign into Russia.
insights.locator: The most important avenue runs through Ukraine.

insights.claim: Russia's shadow fleet is used both to circumvent energy sanctions and increasingly as a platform for drone espionage and sabotage, and Europe should move from one-off boardings to a wider campaign that puts Russian energy transit routes at risk.
insights.speaker: Liana Fix
insights.so_what: Systematic seizures of shadow-fleet tankers would disrupt Russian oil exports and could tighten seaborne crude and tanker markets.
insights.quote: its energy transit routes will be increasingly at risk as more and more ships are boarded and seized
